findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: screen_transfer, get_alerts, screen_domain, screen_cve, screen_package · Private data: screen_wallet, screen_transfer, screen_entity, screen_wallets_batch, search, fetch, screen_licence, screen_cve, screen_packages · Public sink: analyze_transaction, screen_transfer, get_alerts · Destructive: screen_domain, screen_ip.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: screen_transfer, get_alerts, screen_domain, screen_cve, screen_package · Private data: screen_wallet, screen_transfer, screen_entity, screen_wallets_batch, search, fetch, screen_licence, screen_cve, screen_packages · Public sink: analyze_transaction, screen_transfer, get_alerts · Destructive: screen_domain, screen_ip

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
